decisions.summary: Read the recipe lines of land, land-batch and land-tooling, the Makefile variables they expand (recursively), and the two push scripts whole. Do not read the whole gate chain's recipes, whose hook roster names scripts it does not call.

Steps the gate chain runs are already items of their own: `$(MAKE)` edges through make_graph, and l7r-gate's gates as STEPS.

decisions.summary: A script's name is a `scripts/<path>` ending in a file extension, with a trailing full stop cut and `#` lines skipped. Globs, directories and variable paths name no script.
decisions.why: How names are parsed is a design choice inside the request. It follows T259-D1 as the block states it (read paths and names, never prose).

decisions.summary: A script is new by name across all the read sources together, base against head. A moved call, or a script already called elsewhere, adds nothing.
decisions.why: A script the landing already ran is no new mechanism, so the register owes it no new entry. This is T259-D3's shape as the block states it.

decisions.summary: Rule-line reading becomes one shared function `rule` used by make_graph and landing_recipes, so a target-specific variable line is not a rule. make_graph's behavior and tests are unchanged.
decisions.why: An internal refactor that changes no behavior. Nothing in the request touches it.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/tooling-state.md gains `covers: landing script scripts/state-sync.sh`, its prose drops the claim that the check cannot see the script, and guards.md, process-decisions.md and audit-register.md describe the new reading and its replay.
decisions.why: This records the register's own entry for the mechanism the fix covers, which is what the GM asked the register to hold.

decisions.summary: Accepted miss: a script that a called script calls in turn is not followed.
decisions.why: Test it against the purpose. T258's failure one level down would be a new script that state-sync.sh or l7r-gate.sh starts calling, and this limit would miss it. Even so, the limit is legitimate. The GM's own words expect a detector that does not see everything and is grown as misses are found: 'after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. The block names no such nested case today (observed 2026-11-26, the replay over 40 landings found only state-sync.sh), so this leaves no known defect, only a possible future miss handled the way the GM prescribed. Following calls literally would ask entries for every script l7r-gate.sh and the guard launcher name, which is beyond the landing steps the task covers. The limit is written beside the rule in detect.rs, where a later miss would reopen it.

decisions.summary: Accepted miss: a script reached by a path not written `scripts/...`. One exists today, sync-with-main.sh's dirname call of state-sync.sh at sync-in.
decisions.why: The one instance today is state-sync.sh, and this task gives that script a `covers:` line. Since a script is new by name across all the read sources, that instance owes nothing more, and nothing the register needs is missed. Reading `)/name.ext` would misread make land's `.../task-starts.jsonl` as a script, and the GM's backfill-as-we-go words cover any future case.

decisions.summary: Not read: what `l7r-gate land` itself runs.
decisions.why: Those gates are already detected as STEPS (`landing gate <name>`), so nothing is left uncovered.

decisions.summary: Accepted: a message in the push scripts that newly names a script reads as a call. No shell reader is built. The escape is AUDIT_ENTRY_OK and the reopener is a false fire in the guard log.
decisions.why: This narrows nothing the GM asked for. It is a design trade-off in the check's precision, priced on a measured replay (0 such cases in 40 landings, 2026-11-26) and given a falsifier. It is a hypothetical, not a known defect left in place. None of the accepted limits has a case today, which is why 'Found and left? none' holds.

decisions.summary: The six scripts the landing already calls with no entry go into T260's backfill (make audits' BACKFILL 254 -> 260) rather than being written here. T260's line keeps its dated 254.
decisions.why: The GM's request plans for an initial backfill, and T260 is that task, so routing the six there carries out the request rather than deferring a defect of T269. T269's fix makes the six visible, and item 5 asks for T269 to land before T260 writes its backfill. Keeping a dated figure as dated is fine.

decisions.summary: make audit's Bypasses section gains a count of plan-gate escapes by each record's held list, printed after the existing 15-bypass listing, which is unchanged; prints nothing where there is none; in a new module audit/held.rs called from runs()
decisions.why: Serves the audit register the GM asked for (2026-11-25: document measurements and what would falsify an optimization, re-audit them); the plan-gate-escape entry needs a count of what escapes actually held. decisions.summary: The count runs over every record in dev/bypass-log/ whose target is 'plan-gate push' or opens 'plan-gate tick ', not just the last 15 listed
decisions.why: Wider than the listing, not narrower; a census of the gate's escapes is what the audit entry's threshold needs.

decisions.summary: Five classes read from the record's shape: held not recorded; nothing held; plan or review record missing with no block; blocks held at a push; blocks held at a tick
decisions.why: The class scheme is not settled by the request or the spec; it is read from the writer (bypass_record, held_row, tick_gate), so each class says what the record says. Labels that gloss classes 1, 4 and 5 (pre-T262, T84's scope) are wording, not a ruling.

decisions.summary: Blocks held are classed by where the gate judged (push or tick), not split into ticked tasks' blocks against the asked task's blocks; a count by owning task would need the tick record to carry the task id, left as a title in the builder's report and not built
decisions.why: Grepped request.md and spec-index.md for held, escape, bypass, ticked, asked, plan-gate and PLAN_REVIEW: nothing asks for a by-owner count, so declining one narrows nothing asked. The by-owner split appears only as the block's own framing of its task line, which the bundle does not carry and this review could not read. Leaving it unbuilt is not a defect: no wrong outcome follows, since each class states only what the record holds.

decisions.summary: plan-gate decide-defer records (DEFER_FORM_OK, the decide lint's escape) are not counted although their target opens with plan-gate
decisions.why: A different escape (the decide lint's, not PLAN_REVIEW_OK), with no held list; counting it would permanently pad the 'held not recorded' class with records that can never say what was held.

decisions.summary: The 1281 existing records, none carrying held, are counted as 'held not recorded' and are neither replayed nor classed by their reason text
decisions.why: The task exists because reading escapes by reason gave a false finding (60% put in a class none of 12 replayed records held); counting what the record does not say as not saying is the request-serving reading, and a backfill was not asked.

decisions.summary: Classes 2 to 5 are shown on fixture records only, since the real log has no held record yet; red-first test in measure::audit::tests
decisions.why: The real log physically contains no record with held (measured 2026-11-26 by grep and jq); fixtures are the only way to prove those classes now. A test that enforces the requested count is enforcement, not scope.

decisions.summary: dev/audits/plan-gate-escape.md is updated to name this count and its classes instead of calling it a reader's query
decisions.why: Keeps the GM's audit register accurate about its own measurement.

decisions.why: A dependency order; narrows nothing.

blocks: ### T265 (451 T251's and T250's "Found and left", 2026-11-26: `docs/building-programs.md`'s dedication knob named a ruling of the GM's that no record holds, in wording the gm-attributions check did not read, and it and 0222's drawing-page comment cited each other; and the check took four kinds of record where his verbatim words also stand in a fifth)

decisions.id: D1 relabel the dedication knob CANON -> UNRESEARCHED
decisions.summary: docs/building-programs.md's dedication-knob claim line goes from CANON to UNRESEARCHED (not GUESS), saying whose default it is, that no record of his words holds it, where the date came from, and that only the Fortune's name is from his notes; the knob still defaults to Inari
decisions.why: This applies the GM's T233 words ('I never made a ruling ... That is what a session told me') to one more such attribution: no recorded words back it, so it is not called his. UNRESEARCHED is the label the GM defined on 2026-11-25 ('unresearched would mean that we know we have not yet checked'), and the block shows that the question itself was never searched. Keeping Inari as a best guess pending the backlog is exactly what that rule says, and it also fits his 2026-10-25 words on choices the research does not settle. The research search is deferred by his words of 2026-11-25 and the research switch.

decisions.id: D2 knob 3 prose: the default is this project's, the Bishamon credit is the notes file's
decisions.summary: knob 3's '(GM 2026-09-20)' tag and 'on the GM's word of the same day' are rewritten: the default is this project's and UNRESEARCHED, and the Bishamon choice is credited to the notes file. Otsuki's Obsidian Portal record (gm-assistant's) was not read
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'NOT a ruling' rule: say whose it is. The new wording claims only what the repository's records show, which is that the notes file makes the credit. It does not say he never said it, so it stays accurate whatever the unread Portal record holds. Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed: drawing Bishamon on Hoshigaoka is unchanged, and only the attribution moves.

decisions.summary: the comment stops citing the doc as its record, says UNRESEARCHED and lists where his words were searched for; the visible sentence is not edited
decisions.why: The comment was the attribution that had no record behind it, and fixing it carries out T233's purpose. The visible sentence already says 'which this project takes as', which credits no one falsely. See D10 for leaving that sentence as it is.

decisions.id: D4 the check reads 'a GM ruling'; the broader form is not taken
decisions.summary: gm_attributions NAMES gains 'a GM <noun>' for the nouns it took after 'the GM's'. Bare 'GM ruling' and 'the GM rules' are not taken: measured, they added four hits and none was an attribution
decisions.why: Reading the wording that let this attribution slip past enforces exactly what T233 asked for (a red-first test, and the real line refused). Not taking the broader form narrows nothing: the GM's words and T233's task line name no such form, and the four comments it would have read were not attributions. Refusing them would be a check refusing good work.

decisions.id: D5 a dated rulings file (specs/<NNN>/rulings-YYYY-MM-DD.md) is accepted as a record
decisions.summary: POINTER takes specs/<NNN-slug>/rulings-YYYY-MM-DD.md as a fifth kind of record. There are two, 269's and 280's, both headed verbatim and holding his rulings as block quotations in request.md's form. Only the dated name is taken
decisions.why: This widens what the guard lets pass, past the three kinds of record in T233's task line, which is the coordinating session's build and not the GM's words. Tested against the purpose of his words (a ruling credited to him must stand on what he actually said), the files qualify. These files hold his verbatim words as block quotations with the session's notes under their own headings, the same form as the request.md the check already takes (and this feature's request.md itself carries session notes in parentheses). Refusing a pointer at his verbatim words would be a check refusing correct work. The seam is the block's own reason for excluding tasks.md: the check never compares words, so file kind is the only safeguard. Taking only the dated name, which is the verbatim kind, keeps that safeguard, and second-hand files stay out (D6). Applied literally, the three-kind list would defeat the request's purpose, because it would refuse attributions that are properly backed.

decisions.id: D6 audit.md, tasks.md and commit messages are not records; no docs/gm-rulings.md entry is minted for them
decisions.summary: second-hand files stay refused as pointers. A comment whose words stand only there names them in plain words and does not call them a ruling. No gm-rulings.md entry is created to turn such a quote into a pointer
decisions.why: This keeps the check as strict as T233 asked. T251's brook claim (marsh-edge words moved onto a brook) is the failure the GM's words describe. Creating a gm-rulings.md entry from a second-hand quote would be the same failure laundered into a record. Naming the file plainly, without calling its words a ruling, is the 'say whose it is' rule.

decisions.id: D7 T250's worded-around comments are counted, not swept
decisions.summary: 8 comments name a rulings file and 18 name a tasks.md or audit file; all stay as worded, and the 8 may now name their pointer plainly
decisions.why: None of them makes a false attribution: they already name the file that holds the words, so leaving them is a difference in wording, not a defect. T233's own design leaves unaudited comments in its baseline, to be fixed by page work as pages are edited.

decisions.id: D8 the baseline stays zero bytes; the check is silent on the tree after the relabel
decisions.summary: dev/gm-attribution-baseline.jsonl stays 0 bytes, and the check returns rc 0 after the relabel
decisions.why: The baseline only shrinks, as T233 asked, and nothing is added to it to hide the new refusal: the line was fixed instead.

decisions.id: D9 the claims round is not run by this builder
decisions.summary: claims-owed and claims-triage are run; impl-drift for the relabeled knob and the 2 claims sent to it are left to the coordinating session to dispatch
decisions.why: The GM said 2026-11-25 ('a builder's claims round split off ... sounds good please do that ASAP'). The round is owed and handed off, not skipped.

decisions.id: D10 found and left: 0222's visible sentence has no label item
decisions.summary: the visible sentence 'which this project takes as the ordinary dedication of a country shrine' is left without a label item. The comment and the doc say UNRESEARCHED, the claim is on make research-backlog, and the item is to be filed by the coordinating session
decisions.why: The sentence is true: it credits the choice to this project, not to the GM, and the default is the project's best guess, which the 2026-11-25 backlog rule allows. A missing label item on a sentence that is already accurate is a gap no reader is misled by, not a wrong outcome. The search that would settle it is deferred by his 2026-11-25 words and the research switch, and the backlog tracks it.

decisions.id: D11 found and left: 22 procedure-doc prose lines with GM tags and no pointer
decisions.summary: 11 lines in docs/buildings.md and 11 in docs/building-programs.md name a GM ruling or carry '(GM <date>)' with no pointer on the line, and the check reads only claim lines. They are not searched here; the coordinating session is to file them
decisions.why: This is an unaudited group of lines, not known defects. The block shows none of the 22 to be false, and some are backed a line away. T233's design treats exactly such a group (the 'about 60 unaudited near-twins') as baseline, fixed as pages are edited and waiting for the research switch. T265 does not change the check's scope over prose, which T233 set. The item has to be filed (task numbers from one writer, so by the coordinating session), and filing it carries the GM's T233 purpose forward.

decisions.summary: The delta check reads one more form of landing step, a script newly called from a landing recipe, named `landing script scripts/<path>` the way the other landing steps are named; the kinds stay five.
decisions.why: The GM's register (request.md, 2026-11-25, the audit register) asks that each optimization and process carry its logic, measurements and falsifier, and that what was missed be backfilled 'as we find things that we missed'. decisions.summary: Read the recipe lines of land, land-batch and land-tooling, the Makefile variables they expand (recursively), and the two push scripts whole. Do not read the whole gate chain's recipes, whose hook roster names scripts it does not call.

Steps the gate chain runs are already items of their own: `$(MAKE)` edges through make_graph, and l7r-gate's gates as STEPS.

decisions.summary: A script's name is a `scripts/<path>` ending in a file extension, with a trailing full stop cut and `#` lines skipped. Globs, directories and variable paths name no script.

decisions.summary: A script is new by name across all the read sources together, base against head. A moved call, or a script already called elsewhere, adds nothing.

decisions.summary: Accepted miss: a script that a called script calls in turn is not followed.
decisions.why: Test it against the purpose. T258's failure one level down would be a new script that state-sync.sh or l7r-gate.sh starts calling, and this limit would miss it. Even so, the limit is legitimate. The GM's own words expect a detector that does not see everything and is grown as misses are found: 'after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed'. The block names no such nested case today (observed 2026-11-26, the replay over 40 landings found only state-sync.sh), so this leaves no known defect, only a possible future miss handled the way the GM prescribed. Following calls literally would ask entries for every script l7r-gate.sh and the guard launcher name, which is beyond the landing steps the task covers. The limit is written beside the rule in detect.rs, where a later miss would reopen it.
